title: Normalized strict quotient tensor cochains for compatible open models
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an open immersion $j:U\to X$ of Noetherian schemes, with $\ell$ invertible in global sections. Let $C$ be a compatible open tensor context [lem-pur-completed-open-tensor-representatives], using the completed coefficient sheaves $B_W$ and strict positive quotient towers $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1}$. There exist normalized tensor-completion presentations $t_X,t_U$ [def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison], strict scalar-restriction compatibility $sc$, and the strict scalar comparison $r$ induced by $C.coefficients.ordinary$. For every pair of flat-term K-flat complexes $Q$ over $B_U$ and $F$ over $B_X$ representing integral constructible objects, there is a StrictSquare [def-sf-open-tensor-quotient-data] with total chain comparison $C.strictOpen.totalComparison$, scalar compatibility $sc$ and $r$. This includes the two balanced coefficient isomorphisms with formula $(x\otimes y)\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, the coefficient-linear finite gamma comparisons, their scalar-restriction and reduction equations, scalar-unit augmentations, and the strict square and its localized equality. Its upper and lower augmentations equal the first coordinates of $t_X,t_U$ in every level and degree (RoosNormalization). All quotient transitions and signed unbounded total differentials are retained. This assertion does not give integral constructibility preservation, finite-extension identification, or new derived open operations.

proof.text: Global invertibility gives invertibility in each residue field. Use the existing normalized tensor-completion model existence on X and U. Obtain sc,r and their scalar-unit compatibility from the strict open scalar comparison lemma.

Use the normalized balancing isomorphisms on both pairs. Construct gamma by conjugation of the fixed integral chain comparison through balancing and scalar reduction. Fully faithful restriction lifts it to coefficient-linear finiteGamma and supplies all reduction equations.

Define upper and lower as scalarUnitTower followed by balancing. The coefficient formulas give their scalar-unit section formulas. Naturality of scalarUnitTower with tc.chain, the reduction equation, and the scalar-unit compatibility give the strict square. Define lowerRoute by tc.chain followed by extension of lower. Apply transpose and localization to the strict equality for derivedSquare. Finally use total-summand, tensor and sheafification extensionality: the sections formula agrees with the first Roos coordinate supplied by Tensor.canonical. Thus both augmentations satisfy RoosNormalization.

theorem openQuotientNormalizedCochains [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian U]
    (hlX : IsUnit (l : Γ(X, ⊤))) (hlU : IsUnit (l : Γ(U, ⊤)))
    (C : CompletedOpenTensor.Context l E j) :
    ∃ (tensorX : OpenFactorCoherence.Tensor l E X)
      (tensorU : OpenFactorCoherence.Tensor l E U)
      (sc : ScalarCompatibility l E j C.operations)
      (r : ScalarComparison l E j C.operations sc C.coefficients),
      ∀ (Q : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E U) ℤ)
        (F : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E X) ℤ),
        integralOperationsGoodComplex l E U Q → integralOperationsGoodComplex l E X F →
        sfIntegralConstructible l E U (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) →
        sfIntegralConstructible l E X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) →
        ∃ z : StrictSquare l E j C.operations C.strictOpen.totalComparison sc C.coefficients r
            Q F,
          RoosNormalization l E X tensorX
            ((OpenSemilinearTensor.extensionComplex l E j C.operations).obj Q) F z.upper ∧
          RoosNormalization l E U tensorU Q
            ((OpenSemilinearTensor.restrictionComplex l E j C.operations).obj F) z.lower
